Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

will verb

the future: it will rain, I’ll go

also ’ll, won’t, shall (the future), will have, future tense

classical

Cic. Att. 12.2.2: jam tē vidēbō
Plaut. Men. 225c: Jam ego hīc erō.

vidēbō, faciam, erō

the future tense · Wiktionary

I will see, do, be

Latin keeps the future where English slips into the present after “if” and “when”: hōrologium mittam et librōs, sī erit sūdum, “if it’s fine”. For what will be finished first, the future perfect, where English has the present or the perfect: ubi calx cocta erit, when the lime is (has been) burnt. “Won’t”, refusing, is nōlō (see want).

Other words

  • estō, facitō, scrībitō — you shall …, be sure to …

    the future imperative, in -tō, -tōte · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 4: vīcīnīs bonus estō; Cic. Att. 1.12.4: quod in buccam vēnerit scrībitō · Wiktionary

    For standing instructions, rules and recipes: the “shall” of laws and of Cato’s farm book.

Examples

  • Redī citō. — Jam ego hīc erō.

    Come back soon. — I’ll be right back.Plaut. Men. 225b–225c

  • jam tē vidēbō et quidem, ut spērō, dē viā rēctā ad mē

    I’ll see you soon, and, I hope, straight from the road to my houseCic. Att. 12.2.2

  • hōrologium mittam et librōs, sī erit sūdum

    I’ll send the clock and the books if the weather is fineCic. Fam. 16.18.3

  • quod hodiē nōn est, crās erit

    what isn’t here today will be tomorrowPetr. 45.1

  • cibus sum grandium: crēsce et mandūcābis mē

    I am food for the grown: grow, and you will eat meAug. Conf. 7.10.16

  • hoc signī erit, ubi calx cocta erit

    this will be the sign that the lime is burntCato Agr. 38

  • sī rem nūllam habēbis, quod in buccam vēnerit scrībitō

    if you have no news, write whatever comes into your headCic. Att. 1.12.4

See also going to, shall, future, want, if.
